{{short description|Belgian mathematician (born 1972)}}
'''Dimitri Leemans''' (born 1972) is a Belgian mathematician born in [[Uccle]].

== Biography==
Leemans obtained his Licence en Sciences Mathématiques at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] in 1994 and his doctorate degree, under the supervision of [[Francis Buekenhout]] and Michel Dehon in 1998.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Dimitri Leemans|id= 85056}}</ref><ref>[https://difusion.ulb.ac.be/vufind/Record/ULB-DIPOT:oai:dipot.ulb.ac.be:2013/212051/Holdings "Classification of RWPRI geometries for the Suzuki simple groups"], PhD Thesis, 1998, Dépôt institutionnel, ''[[Université libre de Bruxelles]]''</ref>

He is currently professor at the mathematics department of the Faculty of Sciences of the Université libre de Bruxelles.<ref>[https://www2.ulb.ac.be/facs/sciences/math/departement.html "Website of the Mathematics Department"], ''[[Université libre de Bruxelles]]'' {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190310052813/http://www.ulb.ac.be/facs/sciences/math/departement.html |date=2019-03-10 }}</ref> He lived five years in [[New Zealand]] from 2011 until 2016 where he worked for the [[University of Auckland]] as an associate professor. He returned to Belgium after experiencing problems with Immigration New Zealand because of his stepson's autism.<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/feb/16/prestigious-academic-to-quit-new-zealand-after-autistic-son-refused-residency "Prestigious academic to quit New Zealand after son refused residency"], [[The Guardian]], 16/02/2016.</ref>

== Prizes and awards ==
* Agathon De Potter prize for the period 2000-2002 from the [[Academie Royale des Sciences de Belgique]]<ref>Proclamation des Prix de Concours annuels 2003 et des Prix de Fondations académiques,
Bulletins de l'Académie Royale de Belgique 2003, page 405.</ref>
* 2007 Annual Prize in Mathematics from the [[Academie Royale des Sciences de Belgique]]<ref>F. Buekenhout and S. Gutt, Groupe I: Mathématiques. Residually Weakly Primitive and Locally Two-transitive Geometries for Sporadic Groups par Dimitri Leemans. Rapports des Commissaires,
Bulletins de l'Académie Royale de Belgique 2007, pp. 395-397</ref>
* 2013-2016 [[Marsden grant]] from the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]]<ref>[https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/marsden/awarded-grants/marsden-awards-2012/ "Marsden grant awards 2012"], ''[[Royal Society of New Zealand]]''</ref>
* [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]] 2014 Research Award<ref>[https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?awards "Awards and Prizes"], ''[[New Zealand Mathematical Society]]'', last accessed January 16, 2020.</ref>
* 2018 [[Francois Deruyts Prize]] in Geometry from the  [[Academie Royale des Sciences de Belgique]]{{citation needed|date=March 2020}}

== Research ==
Leemans's principal area of research is at the interface of [[algebra]], [[computational mathematics]], [[combinatorics]] and [[geometry]]. He has made major contributions in the study of regular and [[chiral polytope]]s whose [[automorphism group]]s are finite almost simple groups. He has published more than 90 papers in peer-reviewed scientific journals  and two memoirs of the [[Royal Academies for Science and the Arts of Belgium|Academie Royale des Sciences de Belgique]].<ref>[https://difusion.ulb.ac.be/vufind/Search/Home?lookfor=Dimitri+Leemans&sort=pubdate+desc&submitButton=Recherche&type=person "Research papers of Dimitri Leemans"], Dépôt institutionnel, ''[[Université libre de Bruxelles]]''</ref> He is the developer of the [[Magma (computer algebra system)]] package on [[incidence geometry]] and [[coset]] geometry since 1999.<ref>[https://magma.maths.usyd.edu.au/magma/acknowledge/ "Acknowledgements"], [[Magma (computer algebra system)]]</ref>
